The UK and US have a long and evolving alliance that developed in stages rather than at a single moment. Diplomatic relations were first established in 1785, broken during the War of 1812, and reestablished in 1815 [d3]. The two countries are considered to have become firm military allies from World War I onward — as one source notes, "ever since the United States fought at Britain's side during World War I, relations between the two countries have grown so close that they habitually act in concert in war and diplomacy" [d8], with the US entering WWI as an ally in 1917 [d7]. The alliance deepened dramatically during World War II, when the US began providing military aid to the UK via Lend-Lease in September 1940 [d6], and the close personal relationship between Roosevelt and Churchill helped forge what Churchill later coined the "special relationship" [d5]. Some sources trace even earlier roots of tacit alliance to the 1890s or the Monroe Doctrine era (1823), when shared strategic interests began aligning the two nations [d4][d9], while the U.S. State Department notes the relationship has been strengthened through cooperation in both World Wars, Korea, the Gulf War, and NATO [d3].
